Indian Statistical Institute
Admission 2026-2027
Business Rules for Admission 2026-2027 (M Tech (CS) and
M Tech (CrS))
Indian Statistical Institute offers several academic programmes for which admission is offered on
the basis of the written tests or GATE score (as applicable) and interview.
The academic programmes, along with the category-wise intake capacity, can be found on the
online portal:
https://admission.isical.ac.in.
The business rules stated herein will be followed in the academic year 2026-27 for allocating seats
for M Tech (CS) and M Tech (CrS) programmes.
Seats are allocated to candidates considering the following factors:
(i) The category [GEN, OBC-NCL, SC, ST, PwBD, GEN-EWS] of the candidate.
(ii) The position of the candidate in merit list(s).
(iii) The order of preference of the programmes M Tech (CS) and M Tech (CrS) given by the can-
didate at the time of application.
(iv) Availability of seats at M Tech (CS) and M Tech (CrS) programmes.

1
Categories of Candidates
For the purpose of admission, all candidates who qualify after interview should be partitioned into
different categories based on (birth) categories, presence or absence of disability and nationality.
On the basis of such a partition, each candidate is assigned a category tag as given below.
GEN:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals who do NOT belong to GEN-EWS, OBC-
NCL, SC or ST category (or who fail to produce valid GEN-EWS, OBC-NCL, SC
or ST certiﬁcate) and are NOT Persons with Benchmark Disabilities.
GEN-PwBD:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals who do NOT belong to GEN-EWS, OBC-
NCL, SC or ST category (or who fail to produce valid GEN-EWS, OBC-NCL, SC
or ST certiﬁcate) and are Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. Candidates must
produce a valid PwBD certiﬁcate to be assigned this tag.

or ST certiﬁcate) and are Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. Candidates must
produce a valid PwBD certiﬁcate to be assigned this tag.
GEN-EWS:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals of General category belonging to Eco-
nomically Weaker Section (EWS) as deﬁned in Order No.36039/1/2019-Estt (Res),
Government of India, Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, De-
partment of Personnel & Training, and are NOT Persons with Benchmark Disabil-
ities. Candidate must produce a valid GEN-EWS certiﬁcate to be assigned this
tag.

SC:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals who belong to Scheduled Castes and
are NOT Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. Candidates must produce a
valid SC certiﬁcate to be assigned this tag.
SC-PwBD:

are Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. Candidates must produce valid SC

SC-PwBD:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals who belong to Scheduled Castes and
are Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. Candidates must produce valid SC
and PwBD certiﬁcates to be assigned this tag. Thus, candidates belonging to
the scheduled castes are divided into two mutually exclusive categories and
are assigned either one of the tags SC or SC-PwBD.
ST:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals who belong to Scheduled Tribes and
are NOT Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. Candidates must produce a
valid ST certiﬁcate to be assigned this tag.
ST-PwBD:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals who belong to Scheduled Tribes and
are Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. Candidates must produce valid ST
and PwBD certiﬁcates to be assigned this tag. Thus, candidates belonging to
the scheduled tribes are divided into two mutually exclusive categories and
are assigned either one of the tags ST or ST-PwBD.

2
Merit List(s)
Combined merit lists will be prepared for the M Tech (CS) and M Tech (CrS) programmes based
on the qualifying score of candidates in Written Test I and Written Test II (or GATE score, as
applicable), and Interview. The following merit lists will be prepared:
(i) GEN merit list : It includes candidates who are assigned the tag GEN, GEN-PwBD, GEN-
EWS, GEN-EWS-PwBD, OBC-NCL, OBC-NCL-PwBD, SC, SC-PwBD, ST or ST-PwBD and
have obtained a score greater than or equal to the general qualifying score.
(ii) GEN-EWS merit list : It includes candidates who are assigned the tag GEN-EWS or GEN-
EWS-PwBD and have obtained a score greater than or equal to the GEN qualifying score.
(iii) OBC-NCL merit list: It includes candidates who are assigned the tag OBC-NCL or OBC-
NCL-PwBD and have obtained a score greater than or equal to the OBC qualifying score.

(iii) OBC-NCL merit list: It includes candidates who are assigned the tag OBC-NCL or OBC-
NCL-PwBD and have obtained a score greater than or equal to the OBC qualifying score.
(iv) SC merit list: It includes candidates who are assigned the tag SC or SC-PwBD and have
obtained a score greater than or equal to the SC qualifying score.
(v) ST merit list: It includes candidates who are assigned the tag ST or ST-PwBD and have
obtained a score greater than or equal to the ST qualifying score.
(vi) GEN-PwBD merit list: It includes candidates who are assigned the tag GEN-PwBD, GEN-
EWS-PwBD, OBC-NCL-PwBD, SC-PwBD, or ST-PwBD and have obtained a score greater
than or equal to the PwBD qualifying score.
3
Allocation of Seats to a Programme
A candidate will be allocated to a programme (M Tech (CS) or M Tech (CrS)) based on their
category, position on the combined merit list(s) and programme preference.

2. As indicated in the foregoing table, candidates may become eligible for seat allocation in
more than one seat category depending upon their category tag and merit lists in which
they appear. However, a candidate will be a offered a seat of only one category in either
programme (M Tech (CS) or M Tech (CrS)) in a particular round of allocation. If the seat allo-
cated to a candidate is not in the preferred programme or not in the topmost category listed
in the last column of the above table, in subsequent rounds of seat allocation, the candidate
will be automatically considered for upgradation of programme and/or seat category.

Meaning of upgradation of programme. Suppose in a particular round of allocation, a candidate
has been allocated a seat in the M Tech (CrS) programme (which happens to be their second
preference). For this candidate, in subsequent rounds of seat allocation, an attempt will be
made to offer a seat in the M Tech (CS) programme (i.e., their ﬁrst preference).
Meaning of upgradation of seat category. Suppose a candidate with the category tag SC has been
allocated a seat in the M Tech (CS) programme (which happens to be their ﬁrst preference)
under the seat category SC. Also, suppose that this candidate appears in two merit lists:
GEN and SC. For this candidate, in subsequent rounds of seat allocation, an attempt will be
made to offer a seat in the M Tech (CS) programme under the seat category GEN.
Allocation of programme will have priority over allocation of seat category.

3. If there are less number of seats available under a particular category in an academic pro-
gramme than the number of candidates with the same category-wise rank seeking admission
to the programme, then all those candidates will be offered seats by creating requisite num-
ber of supernumerary seats.
4. Seat allocation rules for candidates with Sponsored tag are as follows.
(a) Seats to be allocated to Sponsored candidates will be supernumerary.
(b) The number of supernumerary seats allotted in each programme to sponsored tag can-
didates is limited to 10% of the total number of seats of the programme.
5. Rules for de-reservation of seats are as follows.
(a) If the number of seats in OBC-NCL category in any particular round of seat allocation
is greater than the number of candidates in the OBC-NCL list then the difference will

(a) If the number of seats in OBC-NCL category in any particular round of seat allocation
is greater than the number of candidates in the OBC-NCL list then the difference will
be de-reserved and treated as GEN category seats for allocation in every round of seat
allocation.
(b) If the number of seats in GEN-PwBD category in any particular round of seat allocation
is greater than the number of candidates in the GEN-PwBD list then the difference will
be de-reserved as GEN category seats.
(c) If the number of seats in SC category in any particular round of seat allocation is greater
than the number of candidates in the SC list, unﬁlled SC seats will be open to ST
category candidates. Similarly, if the number of seats in ST category in any particular
round of seat allocation is greater than the number of candidates in the ST list, unﬁlled
ST seats will be open to SC category candidates. However, unﬁlled SC and ST category
seats will NOT be de-reserved as GEN seats.

ST seats will be open to SC category candidates. However, unﬁlled SC and ST category
seats will NOT be de-reserved as GEN seats.
(d) If the number of seats in GEN-EWS category in any particular round of seat allocation
is greater than the number of candidates in the GEN-EWS list then the difference will
NOT be de-reserved.

Merit List to Admission for Academic Programmes
6.1
Provisional Allocation of Seats
1. From the merit list(s), the programme preference of the candidate and the sequencing order
speciﬁed in Section 5, provisional allocation of seats will be made to eligible candidates for
each programme. In each round, each candidate on the merit list(s) will either be allocated a
provisional seat in one of the programmes or put on the wait list, which is common to both
programmes. If a candidate accepts the offer of a provisional seat in the programme of their
second preference, they will still be considered for programme upgradation.
2. Candidates are given a 2-3 day window in each round to ﬁll-in their options:
(a) If a candidate is offered a provisional seat then the candidate has the option of accepting
or declining the provisional seat.
(b) While accepting the provisional seat offer, a candidate will be required to pay a ‘Seat

or declining the provisional seat.
(b) While accepting the provisional seat offer, a candidate will be required to pay a ‘Seat
Acceptance Deposit’ (refundable).
(c) If a candidate is offered a position on wait list for a seat then the candidate has the
option of accepting or declining to remain on the wait list.
(d) Any candidate on the merit list(s) who does not ﬁll in the option by the 2-3 day window
will be assumed to have declined the respective option.
(e) In the ﬁrst round of seat allocation, while accepting the provisional seat or accepting a
wait list offer the candidate will have to complete registration formalities for conﬁrma-
tion of choice. In subsequent rounds, a wait-listed candidate will have to accept/decline
the provisional seat if the offer changes.
(f) A candidate who has declined a provisional seat offer or wait list offer at any round is
NOT considered for the rest of the admission process. Candidates will NOT be able to

(f) A candidate who has declined a provisional seat offer or wait list offer at any round is
NOT considered for the rest of the admission process. Candidates will NOT be able to
change this option. In particular, if a candidate declines the offer of a provisional seat in
the programme of their second preference, they will not be considered for a programme
upgradation.
6.2
Provisional Seats to Conﬁrmation of Admission
1. A candidate who accepts a provisional seat offer will receive by email a Provisional Seat
Allocation Letter which will specify date of reporting, reporting centre and ﬁnancial fee details.
2. Candidates who have accepted a provisional seat or wait list offer should report at a Report-
ing Centre for document veriﬁcation on the speciﬁed date.
3. If a candidate accepts a provisional seat then the candidate’s admission will be conﬁrmed
by the Reporting Centre after veriﬁcation of the original documents and ensuring that the

3. If a candidate accepts a provisional seat then the candidate’s admission will be conﬁrmed
by the Reporting Centre after veriﬁcation of the original documents and ensuring that the
candidate meets all the eligibility norms. Failure to report in person for seat acceptance will
be considered as if the candidate has declined the provisional seat offer. This seat will be
assigned to the next eligible person on the wait list.

4. If a candidate accepts a wait list offer then veriﬁcation of the original documents will be
done at the Reporting Centre to ensure that the candidate meets all the eligibility norms. At
the ﬁnal round, if the candidate is eligible for a seat as per the sequencing order then the
candidate will be offered admission to the programme. Failure to report in person will be
considered as if the candidate has declined the wait list offer.
6.3
On-spot admission
On-spot admissions will be conducted only once in a particular year of admission.
7
Miscellaneous
1. Only those candidates who appear for Written Test(s) and Interview (unless otherwise men-
tioned in the Selection Policy) will be considered for merit list ranking.
2. Filling-in of options on the online portal for waitlisted candidates is free of cost, i.e., candi-
dates who are waitlisted are NOT required to pay any deposit while accepting the offer.

3. Candidates will NOT be able to change their options once submitted.
4. Delays or disruptions in service due to breakdown of admission portals/computer servers
[due to reasons beyond control] shall be rectiﬁed as early as possible and notiﬁed on the
website
https://admission.isical.ac.in.
The decisions taken in this regard shall be ﬁnal and binding.
5. The admission process for a programme will close when all conﬁrmations of provisional
admissions and spot admissions (if any) are completed.
